subject: Scheduling: POC kickoff & rotating hands-on windows (prompt review + load tests)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: POC kickoff + hands-on: proposed time windows for global sessions

Hi Liam / Christina,

Thanks again for the time last week — excited to get the POC kicked off. To make the hands-on working sessions useful for your engineers across offices, we want to run two ~2-hour hands-on blocks (prompt review, routing sanity checks, and load tests) with a short 30-min load/stress run immediately before each block.

Proposed windows (please reply with availability or alternate windows):
- Option A (US/EU overlap): Feb 24, 17:00–19:00 UTC (good to cover West Coast + EU mornings)
- Option B (APAC focus): Feb 26, 07:00–09:00 UTC (APAC morning / US late night)
- Backup: Feb 25, 12:00–14:00 UTC (EU afternoon)

Agenda (attached: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf): quick intro, prompt examples review, routing & fallback checks, sustained token-level load tests. Roles: Tessa will lead prompt review; Jonas will own routing checks; Karthik, can you confirm Dedicated pool capacity for the load run? We'll aim to keep the hands-on interactive — please nominate who from your side will present workload samples (prompts + traffic mix).

Attachments: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf, load-test-plan.xlsx (first pass).

If these windows won't work, we can do a rotating schedule so each region sees at least one reasonable hour. Once we agree, I'll send calendar invites (rotating-timezone naming) and short HubSpot update.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Direct: +1 415 555 0139

Alternatively, Feb 26 08:00–10:00 UTC would work well for APAC + US late overlap.

Also: our engineering lead wants the prompt-review session to happen before the load run so we can iterate quickly — happy to reorder. Can you confirm what duration you need for the load test (sustained vs spike)?

Looking forward to locking this in.

Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 08:22:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on: proposed time windows for global sessions

Liam — thanks for the heads up. To keep this from stretching across too many small sessions, can we commit to two rotating blocks instead of three separate windows? Proposed plan:

1) Feb 24, 17:00–19:00 UTC (we'll shift by +1h to 18:00 if needed — open to confirmation) — cover US evening + EU daytime.
2) Feb 26, 07:00–09:00 UTC — APAC-focused window.

Operational notes:
- Load test: 30-minute sustained run at target QPS followed by 15-minute spike pattern; total load window ~45 min. See attached load-test-plan.xlsx for traffic mix and sequences.
- Order: prompt review (30–40 min) → routing checks (20 min) → load test (45 min) → debrief (15 min).
- Tessa will lead prompt examples and validation; Vanessa will coordinate invites and external RSVPs.
- Karthik: can you confirm Dedicated pool reservation for both windows (estimate: 4x A100 equiv for the sustained phase)? If not, what's the fallback timestamp and expected latency impact?

If that plan looks good to the EdgeCorp/Startups folks, we'll lock times and send calendar invites with explicit timezone labels.

Jonas
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

On Sun, Feb 15, 2026 at 08:22 +0000 Jonas Weber wrote:
> Load test: 30-minute sustained run at target QPS followed by 15-minute spike pattern; total load window ~45 min.

Confirmed — I reserved a Dedicated pool for both windows: 4x A100-equivalent for the sustained phase and automatic fallback to 2x A100 for spike windows (we'll add headroom on the second window if needed).

Two quick asks from infra:
1) Please send target token lengths and average prompt/response size for the sequences we'll use (I flagged the load-test-plan.xlsx). That affects kernel selection and memory planning.
2) If you want quantization profiles tested (int8 vs int4), we need one extra 30-min slot for a quick comparative run — propose doing this as an optional 30-min add-on before the Feb 26 APAC block.

I added a shared calendar placeholder: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123 — I'll attach the Dedicated reservation ID to the invites.
